claim: Crotamiton (N-ethyl-o-crotonotoluidide) showed anti-aging activity when screened using Caenorhabditis elegans as an animal model.
source: While screening our in-house 1072 marketed drugs for their ability to extend the lifespan using Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) as an animal model, crotamiton (N-ethyl-o-crotonotoluidide) showed anti-aging activity and was selected for further structural optimization.
evidence: The abstract states that crotamiton showed anti-aging activity in the screening study using C. elegans.

claim: JM03, a crotamiton derivative with ortho-fluoro substitution, showed better activity in terms of lifespan-extension and stress resistance than crotamiton.
source: After replacing the ortho-methyl of crotamiton with ortho-fluoro, crotamiton derivative JM03 was obtained and showed better activity in terms of lifespan-extension and stress resistance than crotamiton.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that JM03 showed better activity than crotamiton based on experimental results.

claim: JM03 extended the lifespan of C. elegans through osmotic avoidance abnormal-9 (OSM-9).
source: It was further explored that JM03 extended the lifespan of C. elegans through osmotic avoidance abnormal-9 (OSM-9).
evidence: The abstract states that JM03 extends lifespan through OSM-9 based on experimental exploration.

claim: JM03 improves the ability of nematode to resist oxidative stress and hypertonic stress through OSM-9, but not osm-9/capsaicin receptor related-2 (OCR-2).
source: Besides, JM03 improves the ability of nematode to resist oxidative stress and hypertonic stress through OSM-9, but not osm-9/capsaicin receptor related-2 (OCR-2).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that JM03 improves stress resistance through OSM-9 but not OCR-2.

claim: The inhibition of OSM-9 by JM03 reduces the aggregation of Q35 in C. elegans via upregulating the genes associated with proteostasis.
source: Then the inhibition of OSM-9 by JM03 reduces the aggregation of Q35 in C. elegans via upregulating the genes associated with proteostasis.
evidence: The abstract states that JM03 reduces Q35 aggregation through upregulation of proteostasis genes.

claim: SKN-1 signaling was activated after JM03 treatment, which might contribute to proteostasis, stress resistance and lifespan extension.
source: SKN-1 signaling was also found to be activated after JM03 treatment, which might contribute to proteostasis, stress resistance and lifespan extension.
evidence: The abstract states that SKN-1 signaling was found to be activated, with speculation about its contribution to various effects.

claim: Many aging associated signaling pathways discovered in Caenorhabditis elegans are conserved in mammals.
source: Numerous aging associated signaling pathways, discovered in Caenorhabditis elegans, are found to be conserved in the mammals (Kenyon, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kenyon, 2010.

claim: TRPV subfamily proteins are encoded by five genes in C. elegans, including osm-9, ocr-1, ocr-2, ocr-3 and ocr-4.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xiao and Xu, 2009.

claim: Only loss of osm-9 or ocr-2 in worms resulted in the lifespan extension.
source: Only loss of osm-9 or ocr-2 in worms resulted in the lifespan extension (Sheng et al., 2017).

claim: OSM-9 and OCR-2 can form heterotetrameric channels which transduce signals from olfactory, nociceptive, and serotonergic neurons.

claim: The inactivation of OCR-2 extends the L1 starvation survival.
source: It has been shown in previous studies that the inactivation of OCR-2 extends the L1 starvation survival, while null mutations in osm-9 did not alter L1 starvation survival (Lee and Ashrafi, 2008).

claim: Null mutations in osm-9 did not alter L1 starvation survival.

claim: Osm-9 null mutants showed more resistance to oxidative or hypertonic stress than the control worms.

claim: Taurine promoted longevity of C. elegans in oxidative stress condition by inhibiting OSM-9 but not OCR-2.
source: Noticeably, it was reported that taurine, an essential amino acid involved in various physiological functions, promoted longevity of C. elegans in oxidative stress condition by inhibiting OSM-9 but not OCR-2 (Moriuchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Moriuchi et al., 2018.

claim: Crotamiton at 100 μM significantly extended the lifespan of wild type (N2) worms (p = 0.0032).
source: Phenotypic screening led to the discovery of crotamiton as a hit compound for prolonging the lifespan in wild type (N2) worms. Data were compared using the Log-rank test. p = 0.0032 for Cro 100 μM.
evidence: Figure 1a shows lifespan data with statistical significance p = 0.0032 for crotamiton 100 μM.

claim: Crotamiton at 400 μM did not change the reproductive capacity in treated worms.
source: The reproductive capacity was not changed in crotamiton-treated worms at 400 μM (Figure 1c);
evidence: Figure 1c shows data on total brood size with no significant difference.

claim: Crotamiton showed no toxicity to MRC-5 cells even up to 400 μM.
source: For the normal human fetal lung fibroblasts cells MRC-5, crotamiton showed no toxicity even up to 400 μM (Figure 1d).
evidence: Figure 1d shows cell viability data for MRC-5 cells treated with crotamiton.

claim: Permethrin failed to extend the lifespan of C. elegans.
source: However, both of the compounds failed to extend the worm lifespan (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which indicated that the lifespan-extension of crotamiton was not related to its resistance to scabies, but closely related to its structure and target.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1a shows that permethrin failed to extend lifespan.

claim: Benzyl benzoate failed to extend the lifespan of C. elegans.
source: However, both of the compounds failed to extend the worm lifespan (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which indicated that the lifespan-extension of crotamiton was not related to its resistance to scabies, but closely related to its structure and target.
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 1b shows that benzyl benzoate failed to extend lifespan.

claim: The lifespan-extension of crotamiton was not related to its resistance to scabies, but closely related to its structure and target.
source: However, both of the compounds failed to extend the worm lifespan (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), which indicated that the lifespan-extension of crotamiton was not related to its resistance to scabies, but closely related to its structure and target.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that other anti-scabies drugs did not extend lifespan.

claim: Crotamiton showed no significant effect on bacterial growth at 400 μM.
source: Moreover, crotamiton showed no significant effect on the bacterial growth, which further ascertained that the anti-aging effect is not the result of insufficient food (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 2a shows bacterial growth data for crotamiton.

claim: JM03 at 400 μM significantly prolonged lifespan in wild-type worms (p < 0.0001).
source: JM03 prolonged lifespan in wild-type worms. p-values by Log-rank test. p = 0.0737 for Cro 400 μM. p < 0.0001 for JM03 400 μM.
evidence: Figure 2b shows lifespan data with statistical significance p < 0.0001 for JM03 400 μM.

claim: JM03 at 400 μM significantly prolonged lifespan in wild-type worms without FUdR treatment (p = 0.0003).
source: JM03 prolonged lifespan in wild-type worms without FUdR treatment. p-values by Log-rank test. p = 0.0513 for Cro 400 μM. p = 0.0003 for JM03 400 μM.
evidence: Figure 2c shows lifespan data without FUdR with statistical significance p = 0.0003 for JM03 400 μM.

claim: JM03 did not change the body bend rate of C. elegans at different ages.
source: It was found that JM03 did not change the body bend rate of C. elegans at different age (Figure 2d).
evidence: Figure 2d shows body bend rate data at days 3, 8, and 12.

claim: JM03-treated groups exhibited increased pharyngeal pumping rate at day 9 (p = 0.0015).
source: JM03-treated groups exhibited increased pharyngeal pumping rate at day 9 (Figure 2e).
evidence: Figure 2e shows pharyngeal pumping rate data with statistical significance p = 0.0015 for 9 days.

claim: No changed reproductive capacity was observed in JM03-treated worms.
source: Additionally, no changed reproductive capacity was observed in JM03-treated worms (Figure 2f).
evidence: Figure 2f shows total brood size data with no significant difference.

claim: JM03 showed no significant effect on bacterial growth at 400 μM.
source: Similar to crotamiton, the antiaging effect of JM03 is not the result of insufficient food (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Figure 1—figure supplement 2b shows bacterial growth data for JM03.

claim: Knockdown of osm-9 via RNAi extended the lifespan of worms compared to the empty vector group.
source: As shown in Figure 3a and b, knockdown of osm-9 or ocr-2 via RNAi (Figure 3d and e) extended the lifespan of worms compared to the empty vector group.
evidence: Figure 3a shows lifespan data for osm-9 RNAi with p = 0.0028 between Empty vector Ctrl and osm-9 RNAi Ctrl.

claim: Knockdown of ocr-2 via RNAi extended the lifespan of worms compared to the empty vector group.
source: As shown in Figure 3a and b, knockdown of osm-9 or ocr-2 via RNAi (Figure 3d and e) extended the lifespan of worms compared to the empty vector group.
evidence: Figure 3b shows lifespan data for ocr-2 RNAi with p = 0.0084 between Empty vector Ctrl and ocr-2 RNAi Ctrl.

claim: JM03 failed to extend the lifespan of osm-9 knockdown worms.
source: Notably, JM03 failed to extend the lifespan of osm-9 knockdown worms (Figure 3a), but still extended the lifespan of ocr-2 knockdown worms (Figure 3b).
evidence: Figure 3a shows no significant difference between osm-9 RNAi Ctrl and osm-9 RNAi JM03.

claim: JM03 extended the lifespan of ocr-2 knockdown worms.
source: Notably, JM03 failed to extend the lifespan of osm-9 knockdown worms (Figure 3a), but still extended the lifespan of ocr-2 knockdown worms (Figure 3b).
evidence: Figure 3b shows p = 0.0259 between ocr-2 RNAi Ctrl and ocr-2 RNAi JM03.

claim: JM03 was unresponsive to the lifespan of osm-9(ky10) mutants.
source: Consistently, JM03 was found to be unresponsive to the lifespan of osm-9(ky10) mutants (Figure 3c).
evidence: Figure 3c shows no significant difference between osm-9(ky10) Ctrl and osm-9(ky10) JM03.

claim: OSM-9, not OCR-2, played a leading role in JM03-mediated longevity.
source: These results suggested that OSM-9 not OCR-2, played a leading role in JM03-mediated longevity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of JM03 on osm-9 vs ocr-2 knockdown/mutant worms.

claim: The lifespan of C. elegans under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition was significantly increased in JM03-treated group compared with control or crotamiton-treated group.
source: As shown in Figure 4a, the lifespan of C. elegans under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition was significantly increased in JM03-treated group compared with control or crotamiton-treated group.
evidence: Figure 4a shows oxidative stress survival data with p = 0.0001 between Ctrl and JM03 400 μM.

claim: JM03 treatment did not increase the lifespan of osm-9(ky10) mutants under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition.
source: It was shown that JM03 treatment did not increase the lifespan osm-9(ky10) mutants (Figure 4b), but increased the lifespan of ocr-2(ak47) mutants under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition (Figure 4c), which suggested OSM-9 is required for JM03 to improve the anti-oxidative stress ability.
evidence: Figure 4b shows no significant difference between osm-9(ky10) Ctrl and osm-9(ky10) JM03 under oxidative stress.

claim: JM03 treatment increased the lifespan of ocr-2(ak47) mutants under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition.
source: It was shown that JM03 treatment did not increase the lifespan osm-9(ky10) mutants (Figure 4b), but increased the lifespan of ocr-2(ak47) mutants under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition (Figure 4c), which suggested OSM-9 is required for JM03 to improve the anti-oxidative stress ability.
evidence: Figure 4c shows p = 0.0024 between ocr-2(ak47) Ctrl and ocr-2(ak47) JM03 under oxidative stress.

claim: OSM-9 is required for JM03 to improve the anti-oxidative stress ability.
source: It was shown that JM03 treatment did not increase the lifespan osm-9(ky10) mutants (Figure 4b), but increased the lifespan of ocr-2(ak47) mutants under paraquat-induced oxidative stress condition (Figure 4c), which suggested OSM-9 is required for JM03 to improve the anti-oxidative stress ability.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of JM03 on osm-9 vs ocr-2 mutants under oxidative stress.

claim: The motile time of C. elegans under hypertonic stress condition was significantly increased in JM03-treated group compared with control or crotamiton-treated group.
source: In addition, the motile time of C. elegans under hypertonic stress condition revealed by motility assays was significantly increased in JM03-treated group compared with control or crotamiton-treated group (Figure 4d).
evidence: Figure 4d shows hypertonic stress motility data with p < 0.0001 between Ctrl and JM03 400 μM.

claim: Osm-9(ky10) mutants exhibited increased motility and viability upon prolonged exposures to high osmotic environments compared with wild-type N2.
source: Osm-9(ky10) mutants exhibited increased motility and viability upon prolonged exposures to high osmotic environments compared with wild-type N2 (Figure 4e), while ocr-2(ak47) mutants exhibited motility and viability similar to wild-type N2 (Figure 4f).
evidence: Figure 4e shows p = 0.0128 between Wild-type Ctrl and osm-9(ky10) Ctrl under hypertonic stress.

claim: Ocr-2(ak47) mutants exhibited motility and viability similar to wild-type N2 under hypertonic stress.
source: Osm-9(ky10) mutants exhibited increased motility and viability upon prolonged exposures to high osmotic environments compared with wild-type N2 (Figure 4e), while ocr-2(ak47) mutants exhibited motility and viability similar to wild-type N2 (Figure 4f).
evidence: Figure 4f shows no significant difference between Wild-type Ctrl and ocr-2(ak47) Ctrl.

claim: For osm-9(ky10) mutants, the increased significance of the motile time under hypertonic stress condition is reduced after JM03 treatment.
source: For osm-9(ky10) mutants, the increased significance of the motile time under hypertonic stress condition is reduced after JM03 treatment (Figure 4e).
evidence: Figure 4e shows p = 0.0254 between osm-9(ky10) Ctrl and osm-9(ky10) JM03 under hypertonic stress.

claim: For ocr-2(ak47) mutants, JM03 still significantly increased the motile time of C. elegans under hypertonic stress condition.
source: But for ocr-2(ak47) mutants, JM03 still significantly increased the motile time of C. elegans under hypertonic stress condition (Figure 4f).
evidence: Figure 4f shows p < 0.0001 between ocr-2(ak47) Ctrl and ocr-2(ak47) JM03 under hypertonic stress.

claim: The OSM-9 inhibition by JM03 increased the anti-oxidative and anti-hypertonic stress ability of C. elegans.
source: Taken together, these results suggested that the OSM-9 inhibition by JM03 increased the anti-oxidative and anti-hypertonic stress ability of C. elegans.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined results from oxidative and hypertonic stress experiments.

claim: JM03 showed no toxicity against MRC-5 cells even up to 400 μM.
source: Similar to crotamiton, JM03 also showed no toxicity against MRC-5 cells even up to 400 μM (Figure 5a).
evidence: Figure 5a shows cell viability data for MRC-5 cells treated with JM03.

claim: 72 hr cell exposure to JM03 induced a mild upregulation of molecular chaperones genes (Clusterin).
source: We observed that 72 hr cell exposure to JM03 induced a mild upregulation of molecular chaperones genes (Clusterin), and a significant upregulation of Nrf2 transcriptional targets genes (Keap1, Nqo1, Txnrd1) (Figure 5b).
evidence: Figure 5b shows qPCR data for proteostasis related genes in MRC-5 cells.

claim: 72 hr cell exposure to JM03 induced a significant upregulation of Nrf2 transcriptional targets genes (Keap1, Nqo1, Txnrd1).
source: We observed that 72 hr cell exposure to JM03 induced a mild upregulation of molecular chaperones genes (Clusterin), and a significant upregulation of Nrf2 transcriptional targets genes (Keap1, Nqo1, Txnrd1) (Figure 5b).
evidence: Figure 5b shows qPCR data with p = 0.0041 for Keap1, p = 0.0001 for Nqo1, p = 0.0003 for Txnrd1.

claim: Oxidative stress enhances rapid and widespread protein aggregation and misfolding in C. elegans.
source: It has been reported that oxidative (Mark et al., 2016) and hypertonic (Lee et al., 2016) stress enhance rapid and widespread protein aggregation and misfolding in C. elegans.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mark et al., 2016 and Lee et al., 2016.

claim: Hypertonic stress enhances rapid and widespread protein aggregation and misfolding in C. elegans.
source: It has been reported that oxidative (Mark et al., 2016) and hypertonic (Lee et al., 2016) stress enhance rapid and widespread protein aggregation and misfolding in C. elegans.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mark et al., 2016 and Lee et al., 2016.

claim: Q35::YFP is normally fully soluble in the muscles cells of young worms, but undergoes a slow, progressive aggregation as C. elegans ages.
source: Q35::YFP is normally fully soluble in the muscles cells of young worms, but undergoes a slow, progressive aggregation as C. elegans ages (Morley et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Morley et al., 2002.

claim: The anti-hypertonic stress ability of Q35::YFP and wild-type worms was similar.
source: Here, we observed the anti-hypertonic stress ability of Q35::YFP and wild-type worms was similar (Figure 5c).
evidence: Figure 5c shows no significant difference between Wild-type Ctrl and Q35::YFP Ctrl under hypertonic stress.

claim: JM03 significantly increased the motile time of Q35::YFP worms exposed to 500 mM NaCl.
source: JM03 significantly increased the motile time of Q35::YFP or wild-type worms exposed to 500 mM NaCl, which is consistent with results shown in Figure 4d.
evidence: Figure 5c shows p < 0.0001 between Q35::YFP Ctrl and Q35::YFP JM03 under hypertonic stress.

claim: Q35::YFP aggregation was significantly reduced when treated with JM03.
source: Meanwhile, Q35::YFP aggregation was significantly reduced when treated with JM03 (Figure 5d), which suggested JM03 reduced the aggregation of protein in C. elegans.
evidence: Figure 5d shows p < 0.0001 for JM03 treatment on Q35::YFP aggregation.

claim: JM03 reduced the aggregation of protein in C. elegans.
source: Meanwhile, Q35::YFP aggregation was significantly reduced when treated with JM03 (Figure 5d), which suggested JM03 reduced the aggregation of protein in C. elegans.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Q35::YFP aggregation data.

claim: JM03 can upregulate the expression of the genes that play known or presumptive roles in proteostasis in N2 worms but not in osm-9(ky10) mutant.
source: Interestingly, JM03 can upregulate the expression of the genes that play known or presumptive roles in proteostasis in N2 worms but not in osm-9(ky10) mutant revealed by RNA-seq results (Figure 5e).
evidence: Figure 5e shows heatmap of proteostasis genes differentially upregulated by JM03 in N2 but not osm-9(ky10) worms.

claim: JM03 upregulates the genes associated with proteostasis through OSM-9 leading to enhanced proteostasis capacity.
source: Taken together, these results supported the notion that JM03 upregulates the genes associated with proteostasis through OSM-9 leading to enhanced proteostasis capacity, which may improve the ability of nematode to resist oxidative stress and hypertonic stress.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined proteostasis and stress resistance data.

claim: The transcription factors DAF-16 and SKN-1 play important roles in regulating stress resistance, longevity and proteostasis.
source: The transcription factors DAF-16 (Baxi et al., 2017; Li et al., 2019a) and SKN-1 play important roles in regulating stress resistance, longevity and proteostasis (Blackwell et al., 2015; Jones et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Baxi et al., 2017; Li et al., 2019a; Blackwell et al., 2015; Jones et al., 2020.

claim: JM03 prolonged the lifespan of daf-16(mu86) null mutant.
source: JM03 prolonged the lifespan of daf-16(mu86) null mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that DAF-16 is not required for JM03-induced lifespan extension.
evidence: Figure 6—figure supplement 1 shows lifespan data for daf-16(mu86) mutants.

claim: DAF-16 is not required for JM03-induced lifespan extension.
source: JM03 prolonged the lifespan of daf-16(mu86) null mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1), suggesting that DAF-16 is not required for JM03-induced lifespan extension.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that JM03 extends lifespan in daf-16 mutants.

claim: JM03 did not prolong the lifespan of skn-1(zu135) mutants with loss of function mutation in all SKN-1 isoforms.
source: On the contrary, JM03 did not prolonged the lifespan of skn-1(zu135) mutants with loss of function mutation in all SKN-1 isoforms (Bishop and Guarente, 2007), indicating that SKN-1 played an essential role in JM03-induced positive effects (Figure 6a).
evidence: Figure 6a shows no significant difference between skn-1(zu135) Ctrl and skn-1(zu135) JM03.

claim: SKN-1 played an essential role in JM03-induced positive effects.
source: On the contrary, JM03 did not prolonged the lifespan of skn-1(zu135) mutants with loss of function mutation in all SKN-1 isoforms (Bishop and Guarente, 2007), indicating that SKN-1 played an essential role in JM03-induced positive effects (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that JM03 does not extend lifespan in skn-1 mutants.

claim: Skn-1 and its target genes, such as gst-4, gst-6, gst-7, gcs-1, prdx-3, and mtl-1 were upregulated by JM03.
source: We found that skn-1 and its target genes, such as gst-4, gst-6, gst-7, gcs-1, prdx-3, and mtl-1 were upregulated by JM03 (Figure 6b).
evidence: Figure 6b shows heatmap of skn-1 and its target genes upregulated by JM03 from RNA-seq data.

claim: JM03 treatment significantly increased the intensity of GFP fluorescence driven by the native skn-1 promoter (Is007[skn-1::gfp]).
source: JM03 treatment significantly increased the intensity of GFP fluorescence driven by the native skn-1 promoter (Is007[skn-1::gfp]) (Bishop and Guarente, 2007; Figure 6c).
evidence: Figure 6c shows p < 0.0001 for JM03 treatment on skn-1::gfp fluorescence intensity.

claim: JM03 significantly increased the transcriptional expression of skn-1 itself and skn-1 regulated genes gst-4, gst-6, gst-7, gcs-1, ctl-2, prdx-3 or mtl-1.
source: Concurrently, it also significantly increased the transcriptional expression of skn-1 itself and skn-1 regulated genes gst-4, gst-6, gst-7, gcs-1, ctl-2, prdx-3 or mtl-1 (Figure 6d).
evidence: Figure 6d shows qPCR data with statistical significance for multiple skn-1 regulated genes.

claim: JM03 increased the expression of glutathione S-transferase-4 (gst-4) based on the GFP fluorescence signal of gst-4::gfp worms.
source: Subsequently, we also confirmed the increased expression of glutathione S-transferase-4 (gst-4), a key downstream target of SKN-1 (Li et al., 2019b), based on the GFP fluorescence signal of gst-4::gfp worms (Figure 6e).
evidence: Figure 6e shows p < 0.0001 for JM03 treatment on gst-4p::gfp fluorescence intensity.

claim: JM03 did not extend the lifespan of skn-1(zu135) mutants under oxidative stress condition.
source: In addition, JM03 did not extend the lifespan of skn-1(zu135) mutants under oxidative stress condition (Figure 6f).
evidence: Figure 6f shows no significant difference between skn-1(zu135) Ctrl and skn-1(zu135) JM03 under oxidative stress.

claim: JM03 prolongs the lifespan and improves stress-resistance ability of C. elegans through SKN-1 pathway.
source: In conclusion, JM03 prolongs the lifespan and improves stress-resistance ability of C. elegans through SKN-1 pathway.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data showing SKN-1 dependency and activation.

claim: The improved proteostasis capacity of the osm-9 null mutant was due to altered expression of genes encoding components of the proteostasis network.
source: It was reported that the improved proteostasis capacity of the osm-9 null mutant was due to altered expression of genes encoding components of the proteostasis network (including protein degradation, protein synthesis, protein folding and so on) (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2016.

claim: The increased expression of aquaporin-8 (aqp-8) in osm-9(ok1677) mutant was reported by a Germany lab.

claim: The loss/inhibition of osm-9 might help to maintain the salt/water balance to promote proteostasis during the response to hyperosmotic stress.
source: Considering the essential roles of AQP-8 in sustaining the salt/water balance in various cells types and tissues, the loss/inhibition of osm-9 might help to maintain the salt/water balance to promote proteostasis during the response to hyperosmotic stress.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known role of AQP-8 and the observed effects of osm-9 loss.

claim: Osm-9 null mutant showed enhanced survival in hypertonic environments, not due to altered systemic volume regulation or glycerol accumulation and instead may be due to enhanced proteostasis capacity.
source: Osm-9 null mutant was reported to show enhanced survival in hypertonic environments, not due to altered systemic volume regulation or glycerol accumulation and instead may be due to enhanced proteostasis capacity (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2016.

claim: Aging would lead to slower and uncoordinated body movement in C. elegans.
source: It has been reported that aging would lead to slower and uncoordinated body movement in C. elegans (Herndon et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Herndon et al., 2002.

claim: The introduction of fluorine substituents into drugs can enhance biological activity and increase chemical or metabolic stability.
source: Considering the introduction of fluorine substituents into drugs can enhance biological activity and increase chemical or metabolic stability (Hagmann, 2008), JM03 was selected for the following study.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hagmann, 2008.

claim: Crotamiton and JM03 could both prolong the lifespan of C. elegans in the absence of FUdR.
source: Since 5-Fluorodeoxyuridine (FUdR) was used as contraceptive in our lifespan assay and is known to impact lifespan, we also tested the lifespan-extension effect of crotamiton and JM03 without FUdR and found two compounds could both prolong the lifespan of C. elegans in the absence of FUdR (Figure 2c).
evidence: Figure 2c shows lifespan data without FUdR treatment.

claim: TRPV4 channel shows 26% amino acid identity and 44% identity or conservative change to C. elegans OSM-9.
source: Crotamiton is an inhibitor of TRPV4 channel (Kittaka et al., 2017), which shows similarity to the C. elegans channels OSM-9 (26% amino acid identity, 44% identity or conservative change) and OCR-2 (24% identity, 38% identity or conservative change) (Liedtke et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Liedtke et al., 2003.

claim: TRPV4 channel shows 24% amino acid identity and 38% identity or conservative change to C. elegans OCR-2.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Liedtke et al., 2003.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Riera et al., 2014.

claim: OSM-9 is not the only mechanism that mediate the anti-hyperosmotic effect of JM03.
source: It is noted that OSM-9 is not the only mechanism that mediate the anti-hyperosmotic effect of JM03 because JM03 retained a slight effect on osmotic pressure resistance of the osm-9 mutants.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that JM03 has a slight effect on osm-9 mutants under hypertonic stress.

claim: OSM-9 plays major roles in transduction and regulation of signals in several sensory neurons and is important for processes such as volatile chemotaxis and osmotic avoidance.
source: OSM-9 plays major roles in transduction and regulation of signals in several sensory neurons and is important for processes such as volatile chemotaxis and osmotic avoidance (Colbert et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Colbert et al., 1997.

claim: The screening strategy brought a number of false negatives and missed a substantial number of anti-aging compounds.
source: Therefore, our screening strategy indeed brought a number of false negatives and miss a substantial number of anti-aging compounds.
evidence: This is an inference based on the screening methodology and power calculations.

claim: The power of detection of the first-round screen is roughly less than 15% based on power calculation tables.
source: The power of detection of the first-round screen is roughly less than 15% based on the power calculation tables provided by recent computational analysis of lifespan experiment reproducibility (Petrascheck and Miller, 2017).

source: Apart from recently reported verapamil hydrochloride (Liu et al., 2020) and chlorpropamide (Mao et al., 2022) listed in our screening results, crotamiton was finally selected as one hit compound with significant effect on C. elegans lifespan extension in this study (p < 0.01) (Figure 1a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2020.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mao et al., 2022.

claim: Permethrin is a sodium channel inhibitor.
source: In order to exclude the possibility that the anti-aging effect of crotamiton was related to its resistance to scabies, two anti-scabies drugs, permethrin, a sodium channel inhibitor and benzyl benzoate, which exerts toxic effects on the nervous system of scabies (Sunderkötter et al., 2021), were also examined along with crotamiton in the same experiment.
evidence: This is stated in the text with a citation to Sunderkötter et al., 2021.
